## Career
### Singing
In 2008, they sang two songs, "Lost and Found" and "Free Spirit", from the soundtrack of _Alice Upside Down,_ in which they played the lead role. They have also recorded a cover version of the song _Dancing in the Moonlight_ for the 2009 _Space Buddies_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-6)
On April 4, 2010, Stoner posted a video to their YouTube channel announcing the release of their debut single "Flying Forward" on April 20, 2010.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-YouTube-7) Stoner released their debut EP entitled _Beat the System_ in 2011. Also in 2011, Stoner started working with record producers, songwriters and a vocal coach to change their vocal style from "kiddie-pop" to a more soulful pop vibe with a little alternative edge for their first studio album.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-YouTube-7)_[failed verification_]

## Career
### Dancing
After choreography training in Los Angeles, Stoner appeared as a backup dancer in several music videos, notably Missy Elliott's "Work It", "Gossip Folks", "[I'm Really Hot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_Really_Hot "I'm Really Hot")", Eminem's "Just Lose It", and "No Tengo Dinero" by the Kumbia Kings. Stoner was also a backup dancer for Outkast at the [2004 Kids' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Kids'_Choice_Awards "2004 Kids' Choice Awards") and for Will Smith at the [2005 show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Kids'_Choice_Awards "2005 Kids' Choice Awards"). Stoner danced with a dancing group called The JammX Kids between 2003 and 2006. They quit the group in early 2006 due to scheduling conflicts, but continued to work with the individual kids on different jobs. They were also one of the dancers in the special features for the _Shark Tale_ DVD.
Stoner teaches hip hop classes at the Millennium Dance Complex, and is credited as the youngest person to teach a master class there. They also appeared in Debby Ryan's "We Got the Beat" for Disney Channel's _Radio Rebel_. In February 2015, they released a dance tribute video to Missy Elliott featuring a mash up medley of Missy Elliott videos they had danced in when they were younger.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-YouTube.com-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-9) Within the first week, it received more than 12 million views.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-YouTube.com-8) Missy Elliott invited Alyson to perform "Work It" with her at the 2019 MTV Video Music Awards.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-10)

## Career
### Publishing
Stoner was the "dance editor" for _KEWL Magazine_. In February 2009, Stoner released the _Alyson Stoner Project_ described as "a dance video hybrid— melding many styles of entertainment into one package".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-myspace-11) It was directed by Kevin Schmidt, their co-star from _Cheaper by the Dozen_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-myspace-11)
In 2025, Stoner announced the release of their memoir, _Semi-Well-Adjusted Despite Literally Everything_, focusing on child stardom, family violence and religious trauma.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-12) The book debuted at number six on the _Publishers Weekly_ Bestseller List selling 5,579 units in its first week.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-PW-13)

## Personal life
In March 2018, Stoner came out in an article for _Teen Vogue_, stating that they were "attracted to men, women, and people who identify in other ways."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-14) Later that year, they stated in an interview that they did not feel comfortable labeling their sexual orientation or faith at the time.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-15) In June 2023, Stoner came out as non-binary.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-16) They use they/them pronouns. Stoner has stated that they were fired from a television show after coming out as pansexual and queer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-18)
Stoner has spoken openly about their struggles with mental health and eating disorders. They have said that they first experienced anxiety at age six due to the pressures of working in the entertainment industry, with symptoms including heart palpitations, hair loss, and seizures.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-Pasquini_PPL-19) In 2011, at age 17, Stoner was hospitalized and checked themself into a rehab facility for eating disorders, after several years of struggling with anorexia, bulimia, and binge eating. They credit therapy with assisting in their recovery.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-Pasquini_PPL-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-20)

Stoner has stated that they were fired from a television show after coming out as pansexual and queer.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-18)
Stoner has spoken openly about their struggles with mental health and eating disorders. They have said that they first experienced anxiety at age six due to the pressures of working in the entertainment industry, with symptoms including heart palpitations, hair loss, and seizures.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-Pasquini_PPL-19) In 2011, at age 17, Stoner was hospitalized and checked themself into a rehab facility for eating disorders, after several years of struggling with anorexia, bulimia, and binge eating. They credit therapy with assisting in their recovery.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-Pasquini_PPL-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alyson_Stoner#cite_note-20)

**Jenna Lee Dewan** (; born December 3, 1980) is an American actress and dancer. She started her career as a backup dancer for Janet Jackson, and later worked with artists including Christina Aguilera, Pink, and Missy Elliott. She is known for her role as Nora Clark in the 2006 film _Step Up_. She has also starred on the short-lived NBC series _The Playboy Club_ (2011) and had a recurring role on the FX series _American Horror Story: Asylum_ (2012). She portrayed Freya Beauchamp on the Lifetime series _Witches of East End_ (2013–14), Lucy Lane in The CW series _Supergirl_ (2015–16) and _Superman & Lois_ (2022–23), and Joanna in _Soundtrack_ (2019) on Netflix. Dewan has hosted the reality television shows _World of Dance_ (2017–18) and _Flirty Dancing_ (2019) and served as a judge on _Come Dance with Me_ (2022). Since 2021, she has appeared in a supporting role as Bailey Nune on ABC's _The Rookie_.

Dewan was born December 3, 1980[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-bday-1) in Hartford, Connecticut, the daughter of Nancy Smith (née Bursch) and Darryll Dewan, who was a running back on the 1972 Notre Dame football team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-2) Her father is of Syrian-Lebanese and Polish descent and her mother is of Cornish, German and English ancestry.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-4)
As a child, Dewan moved frequently; she mentioned in an interview that she lived in seven cities before reaching the seventh grade.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-5) While attending high school at Notre Dame Preparatory School in Towson, Maryland, Dewan was a varsity cheerleader. She transferred to Grapevine High School in Grapevine, Texas. She was also a varsity cheerleader there and was voted prom queen during her senior year. She attended the University of Southern California and was a member of the California Gamma chapter of Pi Beta Phi.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-7)

Dewan made her first appearance in Janet Jackson's "[Doesn't Really Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doesn't_Really_Matter "Doesn't Really Matter")" video in 2000 and later in "All for You" and the All for You Tour in 2001.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-8) She credits working with Jackson for aiding her career, allowing her to later work with many other artists and giving her the experience necessary to co-star in the dance film _Step Up_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-9) In 2016, Dewan modeled as the face of dancewear manufacturer Danskin in a campaign and photo shoot that captured and featured her athleticism as a dancer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-10)
In 2006, Dewan co-starred with Channing Tatum in _Step Up_, as well as starring in _Take the Lead_ that same year._[citation needed_]
In August 2008, Dewan starred in the Lifetime made-for-television film _Fab Five: The Texas Cheerleader Scandal_ which follows five rule-breaking teens. She portrayed the role of disciplinarian Coach Emma Carr. In November 2009, she appeared in the straight-to-DVD comedy _American Virgin_ alongside Rob Schneider._[citation needed_]
In March 2011, Dewan was cast in the NBC pilot of _The Playboy Club_. In May 2011, NBC picked up the series for a full season. She portrayed the role of Bunny Janie, a provocative Playboy bunny who works at the first Playboy Club in Chicago in 1961. The series premiered on September 19 to 5.2 million viewers with mixed reviews from critics. Due to low ratings, NBC cancelled the series after just three episodes in October 2011._[citation needed_]
In November 2011, Dewan starred in the film _The Jerk Theory_. This was first released in Germany in 2009. It was later released in the United States in November 2011._[citation needed_]
Dewan in 2012

Dewan appeared in the romantic-comedy film _10 Years_, alongside her then-husband Channing Tatum, who also co-produced. The film was released on September 14, 2012. That same year, she appeared as Teresa Morrison in _American Horror Story: Asylum_, the second season of the horror television series._[citation needed_]
In 2013, Dewan began starring in the Lifetime series _Witches of East End_ as Freya Beauchamp, one of the lead characters. In late 2015, she began a recurring role in the CBS/CW series _Supergirl_ as Lucy Lane, and reprised the role in its spinoff _Superman & Lois._[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-11) She also had a recurring role in FOX's _The Resident_. Dewan's 2019 projects include _The Wedding Year_, _Berlin, I Love You_ and _Soundtrack_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-16)
She joined the cast of ABC's _The Rookie_ as Bailey in its third season, and was promoted to series regular in its fourth season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-17)
In 2018, Dewan makes an appearance on the television series _Seatbelt Psychic_ and receives a spooky reading from the famous medium Thomas John.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-18)

In 2022, Dewan starred and executive produced in the Lifetime film _Let's Get Physical_ as part of the "Ripped from the Headlines" feature film. She portrays Sadie Smith who is loosely based on Zumba instructor Alexis Wright with the film inspired by Alexis' and her side prostitution gig.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-19)

### 33andOut Productions
[edit]
Along with friends Reid Carolin, Adam Martingano, Brett Rodriguez and Channing Tatum, Dewan started a production company called 33andOut Productions.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-20) Their first production is a documentary called _Earth Made of Glass_ that follows Rwandan President Paul Kagame and genocide survivor Jean-Pierre Sagahutu. It premiered at the 2010 Tribeca Film Festival.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-producer-21)
In 2006, Dewan started dating actor and dancer Channing Tatum after meeting on the set of their film _Step Up_. They married on July 11, 2009, in Malibu, California.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-cbgwedding-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-23) They have one daughter, named Everly Elizabeth Maiselle Tatum born on May 31, 2013.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-24) On April 2, 2018, the couple announced that they were separating.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-separated-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-26) Six months later, Dewan filed for divorce from Tatum.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-27) Their divorce was finalized in November 2019.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-divorce-28)

### 33andOut Productions
In October 2018, it was confirmed that Dewan was in a relationship with actor Steve Kazee.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-30) In February 2020, she and Kazee announced their engagement.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-32) Their first child, a son named Callum Michael Rebel Kazee was born on March 6, 2020.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-33) On January 17, 2024 it was confirmed via Dewan's Instagram that she and Kazee were expecting their second child.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-34) Their daughter, Rhiannon Lee Kathryn Kazee, was born on June 14, 2024.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-35)

**Jenna Lee Dewan** (; born December 3, 1980) is an American actress and dancer. She started her career as a backup dancer for Janet Jackson, and later worked with artists including Christina Aguilera, Pink, and Missy Elliott. She is known for her role as Nora Clark in the 2006 film _Step Up_. She has also starred on the short-lived NBC series _The Playboy Club_ (2011) and had a recurring role on the FX series _American Horror Story: Asylum_ (2012). She portrayed Freya Beauchamp on the Lifetime series _Witches of East End_ (2013–14), Lucy Lane in The CW series _Supergirl_ (2015–16) and _Superman & Lois_ (2022–23), and Joanna in _Soundtrack_ (2019) on Netflix. Dewan has hosted the reality television shows _World of Dance_ (2017–18) and _Flirty Dancing_ (2019) and served as a judge on _Come Dance with Me_ (2022). Since 2021, she has appeared in a supporting role as Bailey Nune on ABC's _The Rookie_.
texts.1:
Dewan was born December 3, 1980[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-bday-1) in Hartford, Connecticut, the daughter of Nancy Smith (née Bursch) and Darryll Dewan, who was a running back on the 1972 Notre Dame football team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-2) Her father is of Syrian-Lebanese and Polish descent and her mother is of Cornish, German and English ancestry.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-4)
As a child, Dewan moved frequently; she mentioned in an interview that she lived in seven cities before reaching the seventh grade.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-5) While attending high school at Notre Dame Preparatory School in Towson, Maryland, Dewan was a varsity cheerleader. She transferred to Grapevine High School in Grapevine, Texas. She was also a varsity cheerleader there and was voted prom queen during her senior year. She attended the University of Southern California and was a member of the California Gamma chapter of Pi Beta Phi.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-7)
texts.2:
Dewan made her first appearance in Janet Jackson's "[Doesn't Really Matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doesn't_Really_Matter "Doesn't Really Matter")" video in 2000 and later in "All for You" and the All for You Tour in 2001.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-8) She credits working with Jackson for aiding her career, allowing her to later work with many other artists and giving her the experience necessary to co-star in the dance film _Step Up_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-9) In 2016, Dewan modeled as the face of dancewear manufacturer Danskin in a campaign and photo shoot that captured and featured her athleticism as a dancer.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-10)
In 2006, Dewan co-starred with Channing Tatum in _Step Up_, as well as starring in _Take the Lead_ that same year._[citation needed_]
In August 2008, Dewan starred in the Lifetime made-for-television film _Fab Five: The Texas Cheerleader Scandal_ which follows five rule-breaking teens. She portrayed the role of disciplinarian Coach Emma Carr. In November 2009, she appeared in the straight-to-DVD comedy _American Virgin_ alongside Rob Schneider._[citation needed_]
In March 2011, Dewan was cast in the NBC pilot of _The Playboy Club_. In May 2011, NBC picked up the series for a full season. She portrayed the role of Bunny Janie, a provocative Playboy bunny who works at the first Playboy Club in Chicago in 1961. The series premiered on September 19 to 5.2 million viewers with mixed reviews from critics. Due to low ratings, NBC cancelled the series after just three episodes in October 2011._[citation needed_]
In November 2011, Dewan starred in the film _The Jerk Theory_. This was first released in Germany in 2009. It was later released in the United States in November 2011._[citation needed_]

Dewan appeared in the romantic-comedy film _10 Years_, alongside her then-husband Channing Tatum, who also co-produced. The film was released on September 14, 2012. That same year, she appeared as Teresa Morrison in _American Horror Story: Asylum_, the second season of the horror television series._[citation needed_]
In 2013, Dewan began starring in the Lifetime series _Witches of East End_ as Freya Beauchamp, one of the lead characters. In late 2015, she began a recurring role in the CBS/CW series _Supergirl_ as Lucy Lane, and reprised the role in its spinoff _Superman & Lois._[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-11) She also had a recurring role in FOX's _The Resident_. Dewan's 2019 projects include _The Wedding Year_, _Berlin, I Love You_ and _Soundtrack_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-16)
She joined the cast of ABC's _The Rookie_ as Bailey in its third season, and was promoted to series regular in its fourth season.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-17)
In 2018, Dewan makes an appearance on the television series _Seatbelt Psychic_ and receives a spooky reading from the famous medium Thomas John.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-18)
texts.4: In 2022, Dewan starred and executive produced in the Lifetime film _Let's Get Physical_ as part of the "Ripped from the Headlines" feature film. She portrays Sadie Smith who is loosely based on Zumba instructor Alexis Wright with the film inspired by Alexis' and her side prostitution gig.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-19)

### 33andOut Productions
[edit]
Along with friends Reid Carolin, Adam Martingano, Brett Rodriguez and Channing Tatum, Dewan started a production company called 33andOut Productions.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-20) Their first production is a documentary called _Earth Made of Glass_ that follows Rwandan President Paul Kagame and genocide survivor Jean-Pierre Sagahutu. It premiered at the 2010 Tribeca Film Festival.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-producer-21)
In 2006, Dewan started dating actor and dancer Channing Tatum after meeting on the set of their film _Step Up_. They married on July 11, 2009, in Malibu, California.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-cbgwedding-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-23) They have one daughter, named Everly Elizabeth Maiselle Tatum born on May 31, 2013.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-24) On April 2, 2018, the couple announced that they were separating.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-separated-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-26) Six months later, Dewan filed for divorce from Tatum.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-27) Their divorce was finalized in November 2019.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-divorce-28)

In October 2018, it was confirmed that Dewan was in a relationship with actor Steve Kazee.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-30) In February 2020, she and Kazee announced their engagement.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-32) Their first child, a son named Callum Michael Rebel Kazee was born on March 6, 2020.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-33) On January 17, 2024 it was confirmed via Dewan's Instagram that she and Kazee were expecting their second child.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-34) Their daughter, Rhiannon Lee Kathryn Kazee, was born on June 14, 2024.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenna_Dewan#cite_note-35)

## Early life and education
Electra is of Cherokee, German, and Irish descent,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:1-17) and was very close to her family. She said of her mother, "My mom was my rock", and described her older sister Debbie as being "like a second mother to me".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Glamour-18) After Debbie moved to Illinois, Electra said her life "revolved around my mom. She was my best friend, in my life 24/7 whether I wanted her there or not."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Glamour-18)

## Career
Electra started her professional career in 1990 as a dancer at Kings Island in Mason, Ohio, performing in the show "It's Magic", one of the more popular shows in the park's history.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-19) In 1991, she moved to Minneapolis, Minnesota, where she met singer and songwriter Prince.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-stern2000-20) Soon after, Electra signed a recording contract with Prince's Paisley Park Records and made her singing debut with her self-titled debut studio album in 1993,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-21) and would be her only album release.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-22) During her time at Paisley Park Records, she officially became known as _Carmen Electra_.
In May 1996, she was featured in a nude pictorial in _Playboy_ magazine, the first of several. Electra was featured in _Playboy_ four more times: June 1997, December 2000, April 2003, and the January 2009 anniversary issue. She was on the cover of the last three of these issues.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-23)
Electra moved to Los Angeles, where she made her acting debut in the independentcomedy horror film _American Vampire_ (1997). In 1997 she was cast as Lani McKenzie in the American drama series _Baywatch_, for which she achieved her breakthrough. The role lasted a year and helped to establish her as a sex symbol,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:1-17) which has lasted since the late 1990s and the 2000s. In the same year, she began hosting MTV's _Singled Out_.
Electra doing an infomercial for the "Thigh Styler"

## Career
In 1999, she appeared in the Bloodhound Gang's music video of "The Inevitable Return of the Great White Dope". That same year she appeared in the film _The Mating Habits of the Earthbound Human_.
In 2000, Electra starred in the horror-comedy parody film _Scary Movie_ as Drew Decker, a character parodied after Casey Becker from _Scream_ (1996).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Raymond-24) The film was a commercial success,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-25) and spawned the _Scary Movie_ franchise which attained a cult following.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Raymond-24) She later starred as Holly in _Scary Movie 4_ (2006), the fourth film in the franchise, which holds the box-office record for the best opening on Easter weekend.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-26) Electra reprised the role of Lani McKenzie in the 2003 television film_Baywatch: Hawaiian Wedding_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-27)
In 2004, she appeared in the remake of the 1970s TV show_Starsky & Hutch_ (2004), which was a commercial success.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-28) For the role, she won an MTV Movie Award for Best Kiss.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-2004_mtv_movie-29) Electra appeared as characters in the video game _Def Jam: Fight for New York_ and as one of the celebrity challenges in the video game _ESPN NFL 2K5_, both also in 2004.

## Career
In 2005, Electra starred in the family comedy film _Cheaper by the Dozen 2_, which received negative reviews from critics, although it was a moderate box-office success and Electra's performance was praised, with Andrea Gronvall of The Chicago Reader writing that she was "the most winning performer of the bunch".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-30) Also in 2005, she appeared in an episode of _House_ in which she portrayed herself as an injured golfer and farmer. That same year, she joined the voice cast of the animated series _Tripping the Rift_, replacing Gina Gershon as the voice of the android "Six".
Electra in 2005 at the MTV Movie & TV Awards
In 2006 she appeared in _Date Movie_. She occasionally performed with The Pussycat Dolls, most notably as a featured guest of the group when they shared the stage with artists like Patti LaBelle and Debbie Harry on _VH1 Divas 2004_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:0-9)
In 2007, she became a published author with the release of her book, _How to Be Sexy_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-31) Electra continued to appear in parody films, most notably _Epic Movie_ in 2007, and _Meet the Spartans_ and _Disaster Movie_ in 2008. She was featured in some video spoofs of lonelygirl15 that advertised _Epic Movie_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-32) Aside from _Epic Movie_, all of these films were commercial successes.
Electra appeared as a guest judge on _So You Think You Can Dance_ Season 8 on July 6, 2011. She appeared along with regular series judges Nigel Lythgoe and Mary Murphy and fellow guest judge Travis Wall.

## Career
In 2012, Electra joined _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ as a guest judge for the auditions staged in London. She acted as a replacement for Amanda Holden, who was absent due to complications following child birth.

### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
[edit]
She starred in Spike Jonze's directorial debut _Being John Malkovich_ (1999), portraying the pet-obsessed wife of an unemployed puppeteer who, through a portal, finds himself in the mind of actor John Malkovich. The film received widespread acclaim and was an arthouse success.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-37)Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ concluded that Diaz "does a hilarious turn" in her "frumpy wife" role,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-38) and Roger Ebert felt that the actress, "one of the best-looking women in movies, [...] here looks so dowdy we hardly recognize her [...] Diaz has fun with her talent by taking it incognito to strange places and making it work for a living".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-39) For her role, Diaz earned Best Supporting Actress nominations at the Golden Globe, BAFTA, and SAG Awards, however, she was snubbed for the Oscar, which was met with backlash. Her next film release in 1999 was Oliver Stone's sports drama _Any Given Sunday_ (1999), in which veteran coach Tony D'Amato (Al Pacino) has fallen out of favor with her character Christina Pagniacci, the young woman who owns the team. While critical response was mixed, the film made $100 million globally.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-40)
Diaz attending an event for _Gangs of New York_ with Martin Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio

### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
In the film adaptation _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2000\_film) "Charlie's Angels (2000 film)")_ (2000), Diaz, Drew Barrymore, and Lucy Liu played the trio of investigators in Los Angeles. The film was one of the highest-grossing films of the year, grossing $264.1 million.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-41) In 2001, Diaz starred in the Sundance-premiered independent drama _The Invisible Circus_, as a young woman who commits suicide in Europe in the 1970s, and next in the year, she appeared in _Vanilla Sky_, as the former lover of a self-indulgent and vain publishing magnate (Tom Cruise). A wide critical response and commercial success greeted _Vanilla Sky_ upon its release; _Los Angeles Times_ called her "compelling as the embodiment of crazed sensuality"[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-42) and _The New York Times_ said she gives a "ferociously emotional" performance. _San Francisco Chronicle_ similarly stated of the film, "most impressive is Cameron Diaz, whose fatal-attraction stalker is both heartbreaking and terrifying."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-43) She earned nominations for Best Supporting Actress at the Golden Globe Awards, the SAG Awards, the [Critics' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Awards "Critics' Choice Awards"), and the American Film Institute Awards for her performance in the film.

### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
Also in 2001, she voiced Princess Fiona in the animated film _Shrek_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-pay-44) In the film, her character is plagued by a curse that transforms her into an ogress each and every sunset. Locked in a dragon-guarded castle for several years, she is rescued by the title character, whom she later comes to love. The film was a major commercial success, grossing $484.4 million worldwide and became the first movie to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-46) In 2002, Diaz headlined the romantic comedy _The Sweetest Thing_, playing a single woman educating herself on wooing the opposite sex when she finally meets the man of her dreams. The film was a moderate commercial success with a global gross of $68.6 million.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-47)

### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
After completing _Shrek_, Diaz starred in Martin Scorsese's epic period drama _Gangs of New York_, set in the mid-19th century in the Five Points district of New York City; she took on the role of a pickpocket-grifter and the love interest of Leonardo DiCaprio's character. The film received positive reviews by critics and was a box office success, grossing a total of $193 million worldwide.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-49)A. O. Scott of _The New York Times_, agreeing with other top critics on co-star Daniel Day-Lewis's presence overshadowing Diaz and DiCaprio,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-51) felt that the actress "ends up with no outlet for her spitfire energies, since her character is more a structural necessity — the linchpin of male jealousy — than a fully imagined person. The limitations of her role point to a more serious lapse, which is the movie's lack of curiosity about what women's lives might have been like in Old New York".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-52) Diaz next reprised her roles in the commercially successful sequels _[Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels:\_Full\_Throttle "Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle")_ (2003), and _Shrek 2_ (2004).

### 2005–2011: Established actress
[edit]
Diaz at the 2005 Toronto International Film Festival
Diaz received substantial defamation damages from suing American Media Incorporated, after the _National Enquirer_ posted an article and pictures with the headline "Cameron Caught Cheating" on their website in May 2005.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53) The photos claimed to show Diaz cheating on her boyfriend at the time, Justin Timberlake, with the married MTV producer of her show _[Trippin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trippin'\_(American\_TV\_series) "Trippin' (American TV series)")_, Shane Nickerson.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-54) After Diaz complained, the article and pictures were removed from the web and the hard copy did not contain any of the content. The magazine apologized to Diaz, Timberlake, Nickerson and his wife for the distress caused and said the story was untrue and the picture showed no more than a goodbye hug between friends.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53)

## Early life and education
Electra is of Cherokee, German, and Irish descent,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:1-17) and was very close to her family. She said of her mother, "My mom was my rock", and described her older sister Debbie as being "like a second mother to me".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Glamour-18) After Debbie moved to Illinois, Electra said her life "revolved around my mom. She was my best friend, in my life 24/7 whether I wanted her there or not."[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Glamour-18)
texts.5:
## Career
Electra started her professional career in 1990 as a dancer at Kings Island in Mason, Ohio, performing in the show "It's Magic", one of the more popular shows in the park's history.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-19) In 1991, she moved to Minneapolis, Minnesota, where she met singer and songwriter Prince.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-stern2000-20) Soon after, Electra signed a recording contract with Prince's Paisley Park Records and made her singing debut with her self-titled debut studio album in 1993,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-21) and would be her only album release.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-22) During her time at Paisley Park Records, she officially became known as _Carmen Electra_.
In May 1996, she was featured in a nude pictorial in _Playboy_ magazine, the first of several. Electra was featured in _Playboy_ four more times: June 1997, December 2000, April 2003, and the January 2009 anniversary issue. She was on the cover of the last three of these issues.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-23)
Electra moved to Los Angeles, where she made her acting debut in the independentcomedy horror film _American Vampire_ (1997). In 1997 she was cast as Lani McKenzie in the American drama series _Baywatch_, for which she achieved her breakthrough. The role lasted a year and helped to establish her as a sex symbol,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:1-17) which has lasted since the late 1990s and the 2000s. In the same year, she began hosting MTV's _Singled Out_.
Electra doing an infomercial for the "Thigh Styler"
texts.6:
## Career
In 1999, she appeared in the Bloodhound Gang's music video of "The Inevitable Return of the Great White Dope". That same year she appeared in the film _The Mating Habits of the Earthbound Human_.
In 2000, Electra starred in the horror-comedy parody film _Scary Movie_ as Drew Decker, a character parodied after Casey Becker from _Scream_ (1996).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Raymond-24) The film was a commercial success,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-25) and spawned the _Scary Movie_ franchise which attained a cult following.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-Raymond-24) She later starred as Holly in _Scary Movie 4_ (2006), the fourth film in the franchise, which holds the box-office record for the best opening on Easter weekend.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-26) Electra reprised the role of Lani McKenzie in the 2003 television film_Baywatch: Hawaiian Wedding_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-27)
In 2004, she appeared in the remake of the 1970s TV show_Starsky & Hutch_ (2004), which was a commercial success.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-28) For the role, she won an MTV Movie Award for Best Kiss.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-2004_mtv_movie-29) Electra appeared as characters in the video game _Def Jam: Fight for New York_ and as one of the celebrity challenges in the video game _ESPN NFL 2K5_, both also in 2004.
texts.7:
## Career
In 2005, Electra starred in the family comedy film _Cheaper by the Dozen 2_, which received negative reviews from critics, although it was a moderate box-office success and Electra's performance was praised, with Andrea Gronvall of The Chicago Reader writing that she was "the most winning performer of the bunch".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-30) Also in 2005, she appeared in an episode of _House_ in which she portrayed herself as an injured golfer and farmer. That same year, she joined the voice cast of the animated series _Tripping the Rift_, replacing Gina Gershon as the voice of the android "Six".
Electra in 2005 at the MTV Movie & TV Awards
In 2006 she appeared in _Date Movie_. She occasionally performed with The Pussycat Dolls, most notably as a featured guest of the group when they shared the stage with artists like Patti LaBelle and Debbie Harry on _VH1 Divas 2004_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-:0-9)
In 2007, she became a published author with the release of her book, _How to Be Sexy_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-31) Electra continued to appear in parody films, most notably _Epic Movie_ in 2007, and _Meet the Spartans_ and _Disaster Movie_ in 2008. She was featured in some video spoofs of lonelygirl15 that advertised _Epic Movie_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Electra#cite_note-32) Aside from _Epic Movie_, all of these films were commercial successes.
Electra appeared as a guest judge on _So You Think You Can Dance_ Season 8 on July 6, 2011. She appeared along with regular series judges Nigel Lythgoe and Mary Murphy and fellow guest judge Travis Wall.
texts.8:
## Career
In 2012, Electra joined _[Britain's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain's\_Got\_Talent "Britain's Got Talent")_ as a guest judge for the auditions staged in London. She acted as a replacement for Amanda Holden, who was absent due to complications following child birth.

### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
[edit]
She starred in Spike Jonze's directorial debut _Being John Malkovich_ (1999), portraying the pet-obsessed wife of an unemployed puppeteer who, through a portal, finds himself in the mind of actor John Malkovich. The film received widespread acclaim and was an arthouse success.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-37)Janet Maslin of _The New York Times_ concluded that Diaz "does a hilarious turn" in her "frumpy wife" role,[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-38) and Roger Ebert felt that the actress, "one of the best-looking women in movies, [...] here looks so dowdy we hardly recognize her [...] Diaz has fun with her talent by taking it incognito to strange places and making it work for a living".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-39) For her role, Diaz earned Best Supporting Actress nominations at the Golden Globe, BAFTA, and SAG Awards, however, she was snubbed for the Oscar, which was met with backlash. Her next film release in 1999 was Oliver Stone's sports drama _Any Given Sunday_ (1999), in which veteran coach Tony D'Amato (Al Pacino) has fallen out of favor with her character Christina Pagniacci, the young woman who owns the team. While critical response was mixed, the film made $100 million globally.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-40)
Diaz attending an event for _Gangs of New York_ with Martin Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio
texts.9:
### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
In the film adaptation _[Charlie's Angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels\_(2000\_film) "Charlie's Angels (2000 film)")_ (2000), Diaz, Drew Barrymore, and Lucy Liu played the trio of investigators in Los Angeles. The film was one of the highest-grossing films of the year, grossing $264.1 million.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-41) In 2001, Diaz starred in the Sundance-premiered independent drama _The Invisible Circus_, as a young woman who commits suicide in Europe in the 1970s, and next in the year, she appeared in _Vanilla Sky_, as the former lover of a self-indulgent and vain publishing magnate (Tom Cruise). A wide critical response and commercial success greeted _Vanilla Sky_ upon its release; _Los Angeles Times_ called her "compelling as the embodiment of crazed sensuality"[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-42) and _The New York Times_ said she gives a "ferociously emotional" performance. _San Francisco Chronicle_ similarly stated of the film, "most impressive is Cameron Diaz, whose fatal-attraction stalker is both heartbreaking and terrifying."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-43) She earned nominations for Best Supporting Actress at the Golden Globe Awards, the SAG Awards, the [Critics' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Choice_Awards "Critics' Choice Awards"), and the American Film Institute Awards for her performance in the film.
texts.10:
### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
Also in 2001, she voiced Princess Fiona in the animated film _Shrek_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-pay-44) In the film, her character is plagued by a curse that transforms her into an ogress each and every sunset. Locked in a dragon-guarded castle for several years, she is rescued by the title character, whom she later comes to love. The film was a major commercial success, grossing $484.4 million worldwide and became the first movie to win the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-46) In 2002, Diaz headlined the romantic comedy _The Sweetest Thing_, playing a single woman educating herself on wooing the opposite sex when she finally meets the man of her dreams. The film was a moderate commercial success with a global gross of $68.6 million.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-47)
texts.11:
### 1999–2004: Dramatic roles and critical success
After completing _Shrek_, Diaz starred in Martin Scorsese's epic period drama _Gangs of New York_, set in the mid-19th century in the Five Points district of New York City; she took on the role of a pickpocket-grifter and the love interest of Leonardo DiCaprio's character. The film received positive reviews by critics and was a box office success, grossing a total of $193 million worldwide.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-49)A. O. Scott of _The New York Times_, agreeing with other top critics on co-star Daniel Day-Lewis's presence overshadowing Diaz and DiCaprio,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-51) felt that the actress "ends up with no outlet for her spitfire energies, since her character is more a structural necessity — the linchpin of male jealousy — than a fully imagined person. The limitations of her role point to a more serious lapse, which is the movie's lack of curiosity about what women's lives might have been like in Old New York".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-52) Diaz next reprised her roles in the commercially successful sequels _[Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie's\_Angels:\_Full\_Throttle "Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle")_ (2003), and _Shrek 2_ (2004).
texts.12:
### 2005–2011: Established actress
[edit]
Diaz at the 2005 Toronto International Film Festival
Diaz received substantial defamation damages from suing American Media Incorporated, after the _National Enquirer_ posted an article and pictures with the headline "Cameron Caught Cheating" on their website in May 2005.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53) The photos claimed to show Diaz cheating on her boyfriend at the time, Justin Timberlake, with the married MTV producer of her show _[Trippin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trippin'\_(American\_TV\_series) "Trippin' (American TV series)")_, Shane Nickerson.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-54) After Diaz complained, the article and pictures were removed from the web and the hard copy did not contain any of the content. The magazine apologized to Diaz, Timberlake, Nickerson and his wife for the distress caused and said the story was untrue and the picture showed no more than a goodbye hug between friends.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz#cite_note-BBC-53)

In 2004, Lohan had lead roles in two major motion pictures. ## Early life
Sullivan, was a co-founder of the Pro-life Party on Long Island.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-sullivaninfo-20) She began home-schooling in grade 11.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rising-21) Lohan's parents married in 1985, separated when she was three, and later reunited.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-ap20070806-17)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-22) They separated again in 2005 and finalized their divorce in 2007.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-sep-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-div-24)
texts.6:
## Career
### Early career and breakthrough (1989–2002)
Lohan began her career as a child model with Ford Models at the age of three.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rsbio-26) She modeled for Calvin Klein Kids and Abercrombie, and appeared in over 60 television commercials for brands like Pizza Hut and [Wendy's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy's "Wendy's"), as well as a Jell-O spot with Bill Cosby.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rsbio-26) One her first roles was playing Chrissie in a 1993 episode of the television soap opera _Guiding Light_. By the age of 10, when Lohan played Alexandra "Alli" Fowler in the soap opera _Another World_, _Soap Opera Magazine_ said she was already considered a show-business veteran.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rsbio-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-27)
texts.7:
## Career
### Early career and breakthrough (1989–2002)
Lohan remained in her role on _Another World_ for a year, before leaving to star in Disney's 1998 family comedy _The Parent Trap_, a remake of the 1961 movie. She played the dual roles of twins, separated in infancy, who try to reunite their long-divorced parents, played by Dennis Quaid and Natasha Richardson.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-wills-28)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-29) The film earned $92 million worldwide and received largely positive reviews.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-tptbox-30)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-31) Lohan received unanimous acclaim for her debut performance.
texts.8:
## Career
### Early career and breakthrough (1989–2002)
Critic Kenneth Turan called Lohan "the soul of this film as much as Hayley Mills was of the original", going on to say that "she is more adept than her predecessor at creating two distinct personalities."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-turan-32) The film won Lohan a Young Artist Award for best performance in a feature film as well as a three-film contract with Disney.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rsbio-26)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-33) At the age of 14, Lohan played Bette Midler's daughter in the pilot episode of the short-lived series _Bette_, but she resigned her role when the production moved from New York to Los Angeles.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-wills-28)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-Biography.com-34) Lohan starred in two made-for-TV movies: _Life-Size_ alongside Tyra Banks in 2000, and _Get a Clue_ in 2002.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-peoplebio-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-rsbio-26)Emilio Estefan and his wife, Gloria Estefan, signed Lohan to a five-album production deal in September 2002.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-35)
texts.9:
## Career
### Rise to prominence (2003–2005)
In 2003, Lohan starred alongside Jamie Lee Curtis in the remake of Disney's family comedy _Freaky Friday_, playing a mother and daughter who switch bodies and have to take on each other's roles. At Lohan's initiative, her character was rewritten and changed from a Goth style to be more mainstream.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-36) Her performance was met with significant praise. Critic Roger Ebert wrote that Lohan "has that Jodie Foster sort of seriousness and intent focus beneath her teenage persona."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-ebert-37)_Freaky Friday_ earned Lohan the award for Breakthrough Performance at the 2004 MTV Movie Awards and, as of 2015, it remained her most commercially successful film, earning $160 million worldwide as well as an 87 percent approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-ffbox-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-40) Her role required her to learn how to play the guitar and to sing. She recorded a song for the film, "Ultimate", which was released to Radio Disney to help promote the film.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-41)
texts.10:
## Career
### Rise to prominence (2003–2005)
In 2004, Lohan had lead roles in two major motion pictures. The first film, Disney's teen comedy _Confessions of a Teenage Drama Queen_, earned a domestic box office total of $29 million, with Brandon Gray of Box Office Mojo commenting that it was "well above expectations as it was strictly for young girls."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-mgbox-42) But the film was not met with critical acclaim.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-43)Robert K. Elder of the _Chicago Tribune_ wrote that "though still a promising star, Lohan will have to do a little penance before she's forgiven for _Confessions_."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindsay_Lohan#cite_note-tdq_review-44) Her second lead role that year, in the teen comedy _Mean Girls_, marked Lohan's first movie independent of Disney.

**Vanessa Joy Lachey** (née**Minnillo**; born November 9, 1980)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-tvg-1) is a Filipino model, actress, and presenter. She was named Miss Teen USA in 1998. She has been a New York–based correspondent for _Entertainment Tonight_ and hosted _Total Request Live_ on MTV. She has starred in two network sitcoms and hosted various competition and reality shows. Lachey portrayed the lead role in the CBS crime drama television series _NCIS: Hawaiʻi_ (2021–2024) for three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)

Vanessa Joy Minnillo was born at the 13th Air Force Regional Medical Center at Clark Air Base in Angeles City, Philippines.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-birth-4) Her father, Vincent Charles Minnillo, is an American citizen who was born in Cleveland, Ohio, while her mother, Helen Ramos Bercero, was born in Manila, Philippines.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-parents'_marriage-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-8) Minnillo has an adopted brother who is two years older.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-9) Her family moved frequently because of her father's service in the Air Force. She lived in Washington, California, Nevada, Florida, Germany, and Japan and attended eleven schools in nine years. Minnillo's parents separated in 1983 and divorced in 1986.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-People_Biography-10) Her mother left the family when Vanessa was 9 years old.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)
Minnillo's parents both remarried. She and her brother Vincent Jr. relocated to Turkey with their mother and stepfather. By 1991, in the wake of Operation Desert Shield, they returned to their father's home, eventually settling in Charleston, South Carolina, where Minnillo attended the Roman Catholic Bishop England High School. From then on, she lived with her father and stepmother, Donna. She has said she had "a very rocky, challenging, and tumultuous childhood."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)

### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
[edit]
Lachey was crowned Miss South Carolina Teen USA and won the title Miss Teen USA in 1998. She was the first Miss Teen USA from South Carolina and also the first from South Carolina to be named the pageant's Miss Congeniality. She was a host on MTV's _The Morning After_ (2003) and _Total Request Live_ (2003–2007)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:0-12) and became a New York City correspondent for _Entertainment Tonight_ in 2005. She hosted _Miss Teen USA 2004_ and _Miss Universe 2007_ beauty pageants.
After leaving MTV and _Entertainment Tonight_, Lachey was featured in print and web-based advertising for Bongo Jeans' Spring/Summer 2007 collection.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-13) She launched a makeup line with Flirt! Cosmetics, which debuted in August 2007 at [Kohl's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohl's "Kohl's") department stores.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-14) In May 2006, _Maxim_ magazine ranked Lachey #15 in its annual Hot 100 issue.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-15) She has been featured on the covers of numerous magazines, including _Maxim_, _Parents_, and _People._[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-16)
Lachey hosting _Total Request Live_ in 2005

### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
Lachey was a finalist in E!'s competition to replace Brooke Burke as host of _Wild On!_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-People_Biography-10) From 2009 to 2011, she hosted ABC's TV series _True Beauty_. The series followed 10 contestants who competed for $100,000 and to be featured in _People_ magazine's 100 most beautiful people issue. The series was produced by Tyra Banks and Ashton Kutcher.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-17) Lachey became a co-host of ABC's game show _Wipeout_ in December 2011.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-18)
Early in her career, Lachey had small roles in numerous television shows, including _[That's Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's\_Life\_(2000\_TV\_series) "That's Life (2000 TV series)")_, _City Girls_, _30 Rock_, _The Bold and the Beautiful_, _Psych_, _Hawaii Five-O_ and _[Maybe It's Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybe\_It's\_Me "Maybe It's Me")_. In 2008, she portrayed Ashlee in the CBS sitcom _How I Met Your Mother_, in the episode "No Tomorrow". She portrayed Amy in the parody film _Disaster Movie_ (2008) alongside Matt Lanter, Kim Kardashian, and Carmen Electra. The film was panned by critics, but was a moderate box-office success, grossing nearly $35 million against a $20 million budget.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-bom-19) In 2009, Lachey and Kardashian acted together again, on CBS's police procedural television series _CSI: NY_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-TV_Guide-20)

### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
In 2011, Lachey had a guest role as Carmen Chao in NBC's sitcom_30 Rock._ She played Tracy in NBC's sitcom _Truth Be Told_ (2015), about two diverse multiracial couples who are best friends, lovers and neighbors. The series ended after one season on December 25, 2015.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-21) On September 6, 2017, Lachey was announced as one of the celebrities who would take part in the 25th season of _Dancing with the Stars_, competing against her husband, Nick. She was paired with professional dancer Maksim Chmerkovskiy,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-22) and Chmerkovskiy's wife, Peta Murgatroyd, was paired with Nick. On October 30, Lachey and Chmerkovskiy became the seventh couple eliminated from the competition, finishing in joint seventh place.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-23)
In 2020, Lachey and her husband Nick were announced as the hosts of the Netflix series _Love Is Blind_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-24) Lachey stated that the show "made literally our dreams come true in terms of being able to work together, being able to spend time together, making our marriage stronger ultimately in the end."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-25) The couple has hosted every season of the show announced to date.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-26)

### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
[edit]
On April 30, 2021, it was announced that Lachey was cast as a series regular in CBS's police procedural TV series _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i._[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-Name_Change_&_Casting-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-Series_regulars-28) Lachey joined the cast in her first leading series role as Jane Tennant,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:3-29) the first female Special Agent in charge of the NCIS: Pearl.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-30) Her role also marked the _NCIS_ franchise's first female lead.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-31) It is a spin-off of the long-running series _NCIS_, and the fourth series in the _NCIS_ franchise. Filming for the series began on the North Shore of Oahu on June 16, 2021.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-33) The series debuted on September 20, 2021,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:3-29)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-34) and was canceled in April 2024. The final episode aired on May 6, 2024.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)

### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
Lachey's first book, _Life from Scratch: Family Traditions That Start with You_, was released on November 16, 2021, by HarperCollins.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-35) Co-written with Dina Gachman, the book includes recipes, parenting tips, birthday rituals, date night ideas, and personal stories.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:2-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-37)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-38)
In 2023, she appeared in General Motors' and Netflix's Super Bowl commercial to promote electric vehicles.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-40) She was included in _Variety_'s "40 Most Powerful Women on Reality TV in 2023" list.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-41)
Nick and Vanessa Lachey at Marquee in Sydney, Australia, on March 30, 2012

### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
In 2006, she began dating singer Nick Lachey after appearing in the video for his song "[What's Left of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_Left_of_Me_(song) "What's Left of Me (song)")".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-44) The couple became engaged in November 2010,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-45) and married on July 15, 2011, at Sir Richard Branson's private Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-46) They were both born on November 9, seven years apart. They have three children, two sons born in September 2012 and December 2016, and one daughter born in January 2015.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-47) Their eldest son was born during the production of the fifth season of _Wipeout_.

**Vanessa Joy Lachey** (née**Minnillo**; born November 9, 1980)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-tvg-1) is a Filipino model, actress, and presenter. She was named Miss Teen USA in 1998. She has been a New York–based correspondent for _Entertainment Tonight_ and hosted _Total Request Live_ on MTV. She has starred in two network sitcoms and hosted various competition and reality shows. Lachey portrayed the lead role in the CBS crime drama television series _NCIS: Hawaiʻi_ (2021–2024) for three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)
texts.1:
Vanessa Joy Minnillo was born at the 13th Air Force Regional Medical Center at Clark Air Base in Angeles City, Philippines.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-birth-4) Her father, Vincent Charles Minnillo, is an American citizen who was born in Cleveland, Ohio, while her mother, Helen Ramos Bercero, was born in Manila, Philippines.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-parents'_marriage-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-8) Minnillo has an adopted brother who is two years older.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-9) Her family moved frequently because of her father's service in the Air Force. She lived in Washington, California, Nevada, Florida, Germany, and Japan and attended eleven schools in nine years. Minnillo's parents separated in 1983 and divorced in 1986.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-People_Biography-10) Her mother left the family when Vanessa was 9 years old.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)
Minnillo's parents both remarried. She and her brother Vincent Jr. relocated to Turkey with their mother and stepfather. By 1991, in the wake of Operation Desert Shield, they returned to their father's home, eventually settling in Charleston, South Carolina, where Minnillo attended the Roman Catholic Bishop England High School. From then on, she lived with her father and stepmother, Donna. She has said she had "a very rocky, challenging, and tumultuous childhood."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)
texts.2:
### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
[edit]
Lachey was crowned Miss South Carolina Teen USA and won the title Miss Teen USA in 1998. She was the first Miss Teen USA from South Carolina and also the first from South Carolina to be named the pageant's Miss Congeniality. She was a host on MTV's _The Morning After_ (2003) and _Total Request Live_ (2003–2007)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:0-12) and became a New York City correspondent for _Entertainment Tonight_ in 2005. She hosted _Miss Teen USA 2004_ and _Miss Universe 2007_ beauty pageants.
After leaving MTV and _Entertainment Tonight_, Lachey was featured in print and web-based advertising for Bongo Jeans' Spring/Summer 2007 collection.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-13) She launched a makeup line with Flirt! Cosmetics, which debuted in August 2007 at [Kohl's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kohl's "Kohl's") department stores.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-14) In May 2006, _Maxim_ magazine ranked Lachey #15 in its annual Hot 100 issue.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-15) She has been featured on the covers of numerous magazines, including _Maxim_, _Parents_, and _People._[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-16)
Lachey hosting _Total Request Live_ in 2005
texts.3:
### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
Lachey was a finalist in E!'s competition to replace Brooke Burke as host of _Wild On!_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-People_Biography-10) From 2009 to 2011, she hosted ABC's TV series _True Beauty_. The series followed 10 contestants who competed for $100,000 and to be featured in _People_ magazine's 100 most beautiful people issue. The series was produced by Tyra Banks and Ashton Kutcher.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-17) Lachey became a co-host of ABC's game show _Wipeout_ in December 2011.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-18)
Early in her career, Lachey had small roles in numerous television shows, including _[That's Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That's\_Life\_(2000\_TV\_series) "That's Life (2000 TV series)")_, _City Girls_, _30 Rock_, _The Bold and the Beautiful_, _Psych_, _Hawaii Five-O_ and _[Maybe It's Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maybe\_It's\_Me "Maybe It's Me")_. In 2008, she portrayed Ashlee in the CBS sitcom _How I Met Your Mother_, in the episode "No Tomorrow". She portrayed Amy in the parody film _Disaster Movie_ (2008) alongside Matt Lanter, Kim Kardashian, and Carmen Electra. The film was panned by critics, but was a moderate box-office success, grossing nearly $35 million against a $20 million budget.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-bom-19) In 2009, Lachey and Kardashian acted together again, on CBS's police procedural television series _CSI: NY_.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-TV_Guide-20)
texts.4:
### 1998–2020: Beauty pageants and television hosting
In 2011, Lachey had a guest role as Carmen Chao in NBC's sitcom_30 Rock._ She played Tracy in NBC's sitcom _Truth Be Told_ (2015), about two diverse multiracial couples who are best friends, lovers and neighbors. The series ended after one season on December 25, 2015.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-21) On September 6, 2017, Lachey was announced as one of the celebrities who would take part in the 25th season of _Dancing with the Stars_, competing against her husband, Nick. She was paired with professional dancer Maksim Chmerkovskiy,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-22) and Chmerkovskiy's wife, Peta Murgatroyd, was paired with Nick. On October 30, Lachey and Chmerkovskiy became the seventh couple eliminated from the competition, finishing in joint seventh place.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-23)
In 2020, Lachey and her husband Nick were announced as the hosts of the Netflix series _Love Is Blind_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-24) Lachey stated that the show "made literally our dreams come true in terms of being able to work together, being able to spend time together, making our marriage stronger ultimately in the end."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-25) The couple has hosted every season of the show announced to date.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-26)
texts.5:
### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
[edit]
On April 30, 2021, it was announced that Lachey was cast as a series regular in CBS's police procedural TV series _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i._[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-Name_Change_&_Casting-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-Series_regulars-28) Lachey joined the cast in her first leading series role as Jane Tennant,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:3-29) the first female Special Agent in charge of the NCIS: Pearl.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-30) Her role also marked the _NCIS_ franchise's first female lead.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-31) It is a spin-off of the long-running series _NCIS_, and the fourth series in the _NCIS_ franchise. Filming for the series began on the North Shore of Oahu on June 16, 2021.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-33) The series debuted on September 20, 2021,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:3-29)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-34) and was canceled in April 2024. The final episode aired on May 6, 2024.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:4-3)
texts.6:
### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
Lachey's first book, _Life from Scratch: Family Traditions That Start with You_, was released on November 16, 2021, by HarperCollins.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-35) Co-written with Dina Gachman, the book includes recipes, parenting tips, birthday rituals, date night ideas, and personal stories.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:2-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-37)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-:1-11)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-38)
In 2023, she appeared in General Motors' and Netflix's Super Bowl commercial to promote electric vehicles.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-40) She was included in _Variety_'s "40 Most Powerful Women on Reality TV in 2023" list.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-41)
Nick and Vanessa Lachey at Marquee in Sydney, Australia, on March 30, 2012
texts.7:
### 2021–present: _NCIS: Hawai ʻ i_ and first book
In 2006, she began dating singer Nick Lachey after appearing in the video for his song "[What's Left of Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's_Left_of_Me_(song) "What's Left of Me (song)")".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-44) The couple became engaged in November 2010,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-45) and married on July 15, 2011, at Sir Richard Branson's private Necker Island in the British Virgin Islands.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-46) They were both born on November 9, seven years apart. They have three children, two sons born in September 2012 and December 2016, and one daughter born in January 2015.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Lachey#cite_note-47) Their eldest son was born during the production of the fifth season of _Wipeout_.
